r4a-wording.imperative: Judge each replacement clause in place, as an agent would: is it true, does it strand anyone, does the two-path grammar survive
r4a-wording.finding: TWO OF THREE QUESTIONS PASS; ONE FINDING. Two-path grammar: GONE, claim verified against the diff -- every 'by default ... otherwise the CLI fallback' framing at the 13 sites is now a single-path sentence, and the only surviving 'fallback' words in skills/ (excl workbench) are unrelated (fail-visibly doctrine, harness permission classifier, cmd-fallback shell marker, map_orient probe order). Stranding: the three F-1 second-checklist sites state the MEASURED truth, not an avoidance of the banned phrase -- I reproduced the refusal myself in a fresh git-backed process (spine_bind while holding own lease -> 'one door drives one spine at a time'; after release -> succeeds), which is exactly what interrogator/SKILL.md:28 and both write-a-skill templates now assert. FINDING (truth, 10 bound-spine sites): the replacements assert the door 'reads its own spine and session from the process environment' AT init -- but at Explorer/Charter/Admiral init the spine does not exist until init_work_area.py runs inside that same imperative, so SPINE_FILE cannot have named it at server start and the door is provably unbound at the moment the sentence is read. Measured: an unbound door returns 'REFUSED: no spine is bound to this door ... Call spine_bind ... or spine_open ...'. So no agent is silently stranded -- the failure is visible and self-describing, which satisfies global-everyone 'fail visibly, no hidden fallback' -- but the corpus no longer carries the first move. grep spine_open/spine_bind over skills/ excluding workbench: ZERO hits; the single corpus mention is workbench/references/checklist-engine.md:34 (lane D2's file), and it names only spine_open (mint), never spine_bind (adopt existing), which is the case these sites are actually in.
